project.title: Sight and Sound
project.maker: Pentagram / Marina Willer and team for the British Film Institute
project.format: A print-and-digital redesign for the British Film Institute's film magazine, using clapperboard-derived grids, typographic contrast, and section color to pace dense cinema coverage

why: A strong editorial-system reference because one structural metaphor—the clapperboard—governs page rhythm, cover behavior, typography, and digital extension without making every section look the same.

compositions.title: Visible grids turn a film-production cue into editorial pacing
compositions.study: Pentagram grounds the magazine's design language in film clapperboards, using bold type and visible grids to create contrast in pace across editorial pages.
compositions.reuse: Choose one domain-specific structural metaphor when a publication needs an ownable grid logic; let it regulate hierarchy and tempo rather than become decorative wallpaper.

compositions.title: A stable masthead flexes with the issue's content color
compositions.study: Section backgrounds signpost the magazine's content, while the cover masthead changes color according to the issue's subject matter.
compositions.reuse: Keep the wordmark geometry stable and vary a constrained color field when recurring issues need freshness without losing shelf recognition.

compositions.title: Feature typography can rotate and crop to change reading speed
compositions.study: Opening spreads juxtapose imagery and type through full-bleed, cropped, and circular image treatments; some headlines run vertically for added impact.
compositions.reuse: Reserve rotation, overscale, and image cropping for feature openers so they signal a deliberate change of pace without weakening ordinary article readability.

assets.role: A reworked historical mark connects a contemporary system to the magazine's legacy
assets.notes: The redesigned logo revisits a 1970s direction with Aldo Novarese's Eurostile and spells out 'and' rather than using an ampersand.
assets.reuse: When renewing a long-running publication, identify one historical typographic cue worth carrying forward and redraw it for current use instead of recreating the archive wholesale.

assets.role: Condensed display type and a readable serif create cinematic tension
assets.notes: The system pairs condensed and semi-condensed 205TF Plaak for headlines with Matthew Carter's Big Caslon for body copy.
assets.reuse: Pair a highly directional display face with a calmer reading face when a magazine needs dramatic section openers without sacrificing sustained reading.

assets.role: Black anchors the identity while a secondary palette classifies content
assets.notes: Black is used across brand communications alongside a complementary palette; colored backgrounds distinguish sections and masthead states.
assets.reuse: Use one semantically resonant neutral as the identity base, then give a small supporting palette a specific navigational job.

interactions.title: Print identity extends into timely digital criticism
interactions.study: Pentagram documents social and digital channels supporting the print publication with real-time reviews and commentary.
interactions.reuse: Treat digital channels as a complementary reading mode with their own cadence; do not assume that a print spread becomes a web page unchanged.

implementation.format: Print-and-digital editorial redesign for a film publication, built from a clapperboard-inspired grid, bold headline treatment, a heritage-aware wordmark, and section coding.
implementation.notes: The official Pentagram case study provides enough detail about the visual metaphor, typography, image treatment, section palette, cover variation, and digital extension for an accepted artifact-study. This entry records those principles only; it does not include magazine artwork, fonts, or source assets.
